mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months indicates significant labor market slack, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% over two consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY change < -3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months indicates a coordinated weakening in demand sectors, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals a deep monetary easing and deflationary environment, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower borrowing costs and stimulus effects.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes compared to non-triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both above 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).
